trade.safety.p: Scammers actively target this community. Four habits stop nearly all of them:
trade.safety.r1p: Never type your seed phrase into any website or share it with anyone: no admin, no support, no exceptions. Whoever has it owns everything.
trade.safety.r2p: Team members never DM first. "Support", giveaways and urgent wallet fixes arriving in your DMs are impersonators. Verify in the public Discord.
trade.safety.r3p: Every wallet popup spends or approves something. If any site asks you to "validate", "sync" or "migrate" your wallet, close it. We'll never ask that.
trade.safety.r4p: Phishing sites clone real ones. Reach marketplaces by typing the address or via the official Discord links channel, never from a DM'd link.

trade.lead: Browse Creatures for sale, then buy, sell or move them straight from your own wallet: no middleman, no custody.
trade.fineprint: You keep custody: your own wallet signs every transaction on Immutable zkEVM, and this site never holds your Creatures or funds. Cashing out is the one place where the route you pick can pass your ETH through someone else on the way to Ethereum, and the route picker says which does what. It's open source, and you can only trade Creatures held in a self-custody wallet like MetaMask. If yours are in Immutable Passport, withdraw them first. You'll need a little IMX for network gas.

trade.xfer.imx.what.h: Everything here moves on Immutable zkEVM
trade.xfer.imx.what.p: That makes it perfect for topping up a second wallet or paying a middleman: a wallet with no IMX can't move a Creature at all. It also means these are not the same tokens an exchange expects. Send to a wallet you control, or to someone you've agreed the network with.

hero.subtitle: What HCC is, how Creatures and LAND came together, and how the new Player Council gives holders a say in creative decisions.
intro.h2: Hold either one, and you're in
intro.lead: Highrise's 11,111 creature avatars and its LAND parcels sit in the same family. Own any one of them and you're a member: Creature Coins every day, wearable looks, exclusive drops and members-only spaces built into Highrise.
intro.stat2: ways in: a Creature or a LAND plot
intro.stat3: fee on the club's own marketplace
s1.h2: So… what is the Creature Club?
s1.lead: The Highrise Creature Club is built from two collectible NFT concepts: 11,111 one-of-a-kind creature avatars and the Highrise LAND NFTs we brought into the same club. Hold either one and you're a member, with perks built into Highrise.
s1.nft.p: Think of an NFT as a one-of-a-kind digital collectible that's genuinely yours, recorded on the blockchain, not just sitting inside an app. Your Creature is yours to keep, wear, sell, or gift, and no one can copy or take it.
s1.cc.p: It's 11,111 unique creature avatars, plus the Highrise LAND parcels folded into the same family. Members unlock wearable looks, daily Creature Coins, exclusive drops, and members-only spaces built into Highrise.
s1.cc.note: Gen 2 is on the way: every LAND will receive its own Creature, and every Gen 1 Creature its own pet, so Creatures and LAND end up equal in perks.
s1.join.h: How do I become a member?
s1.join.p: Just own a Creature or a LAND NFT. That's the whole requirement. Either one grants full Creature Club status: daily Creature Coins, exclusive drops, and the private community spaces.
s1.join.note: Your Discord role is automatic. Once your NFT sits in a wallet linked to your Highrise account, your roles update on their own, usually within an hour. Nothing to claim on your side.
s1.p1p: Every item on your creature is yours to wear inside Highrise.
s1.p2p: Earn coins daily to spin exclusive grabs only members can reach.
s1.p3p: Early and free access to fresh creature content as it ships.
s1.p4p: An exclusive club room and a seat at the community table.
land.perks.summary: LAND owners earn Creature Coins (Premium plots at 3×), get room capacity boosts, keep their slime pets, and take part in the same drops and giveaways as Creature holders.
land.body: LAND NFTs are the club's collection of virtual parcels in the Highrise universe, in Standard and Premium tiers. Most LAND owners also have an adorable slime pet to go with their plot. LAND's original standalone plan changed, so we folded the project into the Creature Club family: owning LAND now makes you a member too.
land.p1p: Your pet stays yours, a collectible creature companion all its own.
land.p2p: Link a plot to a room to raise its capacity: 75 for Standard, 120 for Premium.
land.p3p: Premium LAND earns triple the Creature Coins of Standard, like Legendary creatures do.
land.p4p: LAND NFT owners now earn Creature Coins and join in club drops and giveaways.
journey.lead: Where the club has been, and where it's headed.
t1.p: HCC launches as Highrise's first collectible avatar project: computer-generated creatures, each with a wearable set of items and a promise of perks for holders.
t2.p: LAND launches as virtual parcels of the Highrise universe, in Standard and Premium tiers, with daily Land Tokens, room capacity boosts, an exclusive shop, and slime pets. The original dream: custom, monetizable corners of Highrise you could run yourself.
t3.p: Lots of ambition across both projects, but consistency, communication and follow-through didn't meet the standard holders deserved. We heard the frustration.
t4.p: We wound down the original "custom monetizable Highrise" plan for LAND and brought LAND owners into Creature Club benefits. We converted Land Tokens to Creature Coins, pets stayed with their owners, Premium LAND mirrored higher-tier Creature benefits at 3×, and a compensation path covered owners who didn't want the new direction.
t5.h: LAND benefits become real HCC benefits
t5.p: Regular updates confirmed the practical merge: Discord access opened to LAND owners, Highrise+ eligibility and Creature Coins applied to eligible players, exclusive LAND and Creature giveaways continued, and Gen 2 / shop work moved forward under one HCC update rhythm.
t6.p: A dedicated artist put permanently on finishing Gen 1 & Gen 2. Updates every two weeks. Monthly shop refreshes. Quarterly drops. A clear commitment to communication, delivery, and rebuilding trust.
t7.p: The next step: a holder-led Player Council that helps shape what gets made, across Creatures and LAND alike. Head to the Council page to see how it works.
honest.p: Trust doesn't come back from promises. It comes from consistent delivery and from actually listening. The Council exists so HCC holders aren't just told what's coming next, but help decide it. It's a sounding board with influence on creative direction, run alongside the team that builds.
unify.h2: One club: Creatures + LAND, together
unify.lead: For a long time, Creatures and LAND lived as two separate NFT projects with two separate stories. The goal now is to unify them into a single Creature Club concept: one community, one set of benefits, one roadmap, and one holder voice.
unify.p1p: Land Tokens became Creature Coins, so everyone earns and spends the same way.
unify.p2p: Hold a Creature NFT or LAND NFT and you're a full member with the same core perks.
unify.p3p: Drops, Gen 2 and shop updates serve the whole club, not two parallel tracks.
unify.p4p: The Player Council represents Creature and LAND holders alike.
unify.note: Your assets don't change. Your creature, your LAND plot, and your slime pet stay exactly as they are. Unifying is about the experience around them: one family that's easier to grow, support and build for.
council.member.note: Every HCC holder, Creature or LAND, is a member. Hold for 3 months and you can vote. A Council "seat" is a formal elected role on top of that: only 7 exist, and you vote on who fills 4 of them.
council.lead: A small, holder-led group that works with a dedicated PM and the art team to finish Gen 2 and run the steady drops. It's advisory: a say on creative, not a vote on the business.
council.legend.elected: Elected: chosen by a holder vote
council.legend.appointed: Appointed: 2 from Pocket Worlds + 1 trusted holder
council.fact2: one holder, one vote per seat, never whale-weighted
cboard.lead: All seven seats are filled: four you elected in June, three appointed for continuity. Terms run six months, so this board changes when you vote again.
cboard.group.appointed.meta: 3 seats, 2 from Pocket Worlds and 1 holder
cboard.role.single: Elected by holders of 1 to 4 assets
cboard.role.mid: Elected by holders of 5 to 14 assets
cboard.role.whale: Elected by holders of 15 or more assets
cboard.role.art: Lead concept artist, directing the Gen 2 art
cboard.role.holder: Long-standing holder, appointed to keep the club's memory
cboard.term.none: No fixed term, that's the point of the seat
cboard.foot: Elected seats run six months, two in a row at most, so new voices keep coming through. The appointed seats carry what the Council learned into the next term.
brackets.lead: Your bracket is set by how many HCC assets you hold (Creatures + LAND combined) when the candidacy window opens. Every holder size has a path to run.
brackets.why.p: So the largest holders can't dominate the Council. Every tier of the community has at least one seat reserved for someone who holds at that size. A holder with a single Creature can win a seat.
brackets.run.p: Meet your bracket's asset count at the snapshot, have held at least 1 HCC asset continuously for 3 months (same bar as voters), and self-nominate during the open window by answering the application's open questions on your positions. Brackets gate running, not voting. Every eligible holder votes on all 4 races.
vote.lead: You vote in every seat race, with one vote per seat. The Member race elects two, so you pick two candidates there. The candidates with the most votes win. One holder's vote is never weighted by how much you hold.
vote.p1p: Vote here on the site. Sign in with Discord (linked to your Highrise account) so we can confirm you're an eligible holder.
vote.p2p: Individual votes are never published, only per-seat tallies. You get a private receipt to confirm your vote was counted.
vote.p3p: Votes are final once cast, and most election statistics are published here on the site.
vote.p4p: If a race has no more candidates than seats, you vote to seat them or to reopen nominations. If reopening wins but nobody new steps up, the original candidate is seated. A seat can be contested, never blocked into a vacancy.
vaa.lead: So you can vote on substance, not name recognition, the site includes a Voting Advice Application.
vaa.p1p: Candidates answer a set of open questions in their own words. The tool turns each answer into a clear position the candidate reviews and confirms.
vaa.p2p: You answer the same questions, then see a ranked affinity score for every candidate.
vaa.p3p: It never casts a vote for you: it's advice. The full methodology is published.
power.lead: Some calls the Council makes. Some it advises on. A few it's kept in the loop on. That scope grows as it earns trust.
power.row2: Which creatures & variants make a Gen 2 set
power.row3: The exclusive holder items in each drop
power.note: Pocket Worlds stays the executor and keeps final say on anything touching the economy, brand, or legal guardrails. That protects the whole club.
seat.h2: How you get a seat, and how you keep it
seat.p1p: Hold at least 1 HCC asset (Creature or LAND) continuously for 3 months to vote. To run: 2 seats are open to holders of 1–4 assets, 1 is reserved for holders of 5–14 assets, and 1 for holders of 15+. That way every holder size has a voice.
seat.p2p: A Council seat is tied to you: never bought or traded.
seat.p3p: A self-nomination window opens (you answer a few open questions on your positions), then holders vote.
seat.p4p: Six-month terms, max two in a row for elected seats. Nobody gets stuck in.
rhythm.p1: The PM owns the roadmap and brings the Council clear, scoped questions, each with a "done looks like this" attached. The Council weighs in on specific decisions, not endless open debate.
rhythm.p2: Cadence: a quick check-in every two weeks, plus a live call once a month. Where: a private holder channel to start, with token-gated holder-wide votes for the bigger questions down the line.
faq.q1: Is this a DAO? Do I own part of the company now?
faq.a1: No. The Council is advisory: a sounding board on creative and roadmap decisions. Pocket Worlds remains the executor and keeps final say on the business, the economy and the brand.
faq.q2: Will big holders just take over?
faq.a2: No. It's one holder, one vote in every seat, never weighted by how many Creature or LAND assets you own. How many you hold only affects which seat you can run for, never how much your vote counts. We reserve seats for different holder sizes so everyone gets a voice. Four of the seven seats are elected directly by holders; three are appointed for continuity and competence. We'd rather say that split openly than pretend it's purely democratic.
faq.a3: A dedicated artist is on finishing them, and the Council helps decide which creatures and variants make each Gen 2 set, picking from the options the art team can build.
faq.q4: I own LAND, not a Creature. Am I in the club?
faq.a4: Yes. LAND owners are full Creature Club members. Your Land Tokens became Creature Coins, you earn daily Coins (Premium plots at 3×), and you take part in club drops and giveaways. Your plot and your slime pet stay exactly as they are.
faq.a5: Yes. Plans to migrate creatures off the blockchain have been canceled following Steam approval. If that ever needs to change, we'll tell you early and clearly. No surprises.
faq.q6: What does the Council start with?
faq.a6: It starts advisory-leaning, and its "Decides" power grows release by release as it earns trust, not everything on day one.
faq.q7: How much does a Creature cost, and what if I can't afford one yet?
faq.a7: Prices are set by holders, so they range widely: from a few hundred dollars to several thousand, depending on rarity and traits. For live numbers, the Market page shows the current floor and real sale history. Can't buy in yet? Keep an eye on the Highrise Discord. There are regular giveaways and contests where you can win one for free.
faq.q8: I bought a Creature but don't see my role or perks yet. What gives?
faq.a8: First, make sure the wallet holding it is linked to your Highrise account. That's what connects your NFTs to the club. Once it's linked, your Discord roles and perks sync on their own, usually within an hour. If it's been longer, double-check you linked the right wallet, then ask in the public Highrise Discord.
faq.q9: Where do I buy and sell, and how do I spot a fake?
faq.a9.lead: Start here. The club's own Marketplace lets you browse, buy, sell and transfer straight from your own wallet, in ETH or USDC, with no marketplace fee from us. If you'd rather trade elsewhere, here's where each collection actually lives, so you can check any listing you come across.

gx.truth.h2: What Gen 2 is, and what it isn't
gx.truth.lead: Four things worth knowing on each side. If you only read one part of this page, read this one.
gx.yes1h: Attached to what you already hold
gx.yes1p: Your pet rides on your Creature. Your Gen 2 Creature rides on your plot. The pair moves as one.
gx.yes2p: Gen 2 is what was agreed years ago and never landed. We're closing it out, not selling it to you.
gx.yes3p: There's nothing to buy and no entry to pay. Holding the Gen 1 side is what earns the Gen 2 side.
gx.yes4p: We'll try to fit a pet to its Creature, but plan on the draw being random.
gx.no1p: The Gen 2 half doesn't split off. Sell the Creature and the pet goes with it, in one listing.
gx.no2p: Coins pay per Creature and per plot you hold. Gen 2 doesn't add one, so your daily rate won't move.
gx.no3p: None of it exists in Highrise. Anything sold as a Gen 2 pet or creature today is fake, without exception.
gx.no4p: Sushi is one theme of several. Dessert is already in the works and more follow it, and how many themes there are in the end can still change.
gx.faq.lead: These came out of Discord in the days after update #6. If yours isn't here, ask it in creature-chat and it'll end up on this page.
gx.q1: I own a Creature and no LAND. Do I get anything?
gx.a1: Yes. Every Gen 1 Creature is owed a Gen 2 pet slime, whether or not you hold a plot. Own three Creatures and you're owed three pets.
gx.q2: I own LAND. Am I getting a slime or a creature?
gx.a2: A creature. Plots already have their slime pets, so the Gen 2 side of LAND is a creature attached to the plot. Premium plots get exclusive ones.
gx.q3: Is a new NFT landing in my wallet?
gx.a3: No. Nothing new arrives on its own. The Gen 2 piece attaches to the NFT you already hold, so you end up with one asset carrying both halves rather than two assets side by side.
gx.q4: Can I sell the pet on its own, or keep it and sell the Creature?
gx.a4: No. The two stay together, and that was always the intent: bundling them is what makes your Gen 1 worth more rather than competing with a shinier Gen 2. Vini hasn't ruled out building a way to trade an attached Gen 2 later on, but that's a conversation for after Gen 2 ships, not a plan today.
gx.q5: Do I choose mine, or is it random?
gx.a5: Plan on random. The team will try to fit a pet to the Creature it lands on, so a dark Creature may well end up with something that suits it, but nothing about that is promised and you won't be picking from a menu.
gx.q6: Will I earn more Creature Coins once I have both?
gx.a6: No. Coins pay out per Creature and per LAND plot you hold, and Gen 2 doesn't add one to your count. Buy another NFT and you earn more; getting your Gen 2 half doesn't change your daily rate.
gx.q7: Do rarer NFTs get rarer Gen 2?
gx.a7: Partly, yes. Every Premium LAND plot and every Legendary Creature gets rarer, more exclusive Gen 2 assets. Below those two tiers nothing is settled, so what you've read about holographic Creatures or the ten 1-of-1s pulling special pets is still holder guesswork. When the rest is decided you'll read it here first.
gx.a8: No. Sushi is the first slime theme we've shown, not the whole thing. Dessert is being drawn now, then Nature, Celestial and Elemental, and both the count and the themes themselves can still change as the work lands. The creature sets for LAND are separate again: vampires, werewolves, demons, ghosts, slimes and the Yogurt Zombies.
gx.q9: Why do they look like concepts from years ago?
gx.a9: Because they are, and that's deliberate. The lineup comes straight from the preview shared back then, cleaned up rather than redesigned, because holders asked for the originals before anything new. Slimes were the first pets Highrise ever had and they're simple by nature, so the variety comes from five themed sets instead of five hundred shapes. Plenty of you have said they don't measure up to what the game ships now, and that's fair feedback, honestly given. It's read, and it's being weighed against keeping faith with the original concepts.
gx.a11: There's no date, and we'd rather say that than invent one. What you can hold us to is a progress update every two weeks and a public board per set, so you can watch the work move instead of taking our word for it.
gx.q12: Won't bundling wreck the market if demand drops?
gx.a12: Straight answer from Vini: if buyers won't pay the asking price, the asset doesn't move, and a seller who wants out lowers their price. There's no plan to step into the market and prop it up. The plan is to keep shipping releases and perks so the collection stays worth wanting. Gen 2 is a perk that adds to HCC, not a promise about price.
gx.a13: No. Drops and Creature Store releases carry on alongside it, and pet giveaways plus slime accessory grabs and store items are likely once the pets land. Gen 2 is the debt being paid. It isn't the whole club.
gx.open.lead: These are genuinely open. We'd rather list them than let a guess harden into a fact you trade on.

terms.accept: Acceptance. Voters tick "I agree to the Terms" after logging in with Discord, before their first ballot; candidates explicitly accept at nomination submission. Acceptance is recorded with your Highrise Person ID, Discord ID, and a timestamp.
terms.s1.p: The Council is advisory only; Pocket Worlds keeps final say on business, economy, brand and legal. A seat is not ownership, equity, a security, a token right, employment, or any financial entitlement, and is not a DAO membership.
terms.s2.p: Participation is voluntary and unpaid. There is no employment, contractor, or partnership relationship. Any perks are gifts we can change or withdraw. They're never payment or a right.
terms.s3.p:
Holdings = combined Creatures + LAND at the published snapshot.
  • Voters: held at least 1 HCC NFT continuously for the 3 months ending at the snapshot.
  • Candidates: meet the bracket asset count at the candidacy snapshot and the 3-month continuous-holding bar; self-nominate in the window by answering the application's open questions.
  • Eligibility is assessed against your Highrise account's current primary wallet (holdings across multiple wallets are not aggregated). Snapshots are final.
terms.s4.p: One vote per elected seat (4 seats, plurality). You authenticate by logging in with Discord, which we match to your Highrise account to confirm eligibility. No wallet connection or signing is required, and we never move or spend your assets. Voting is per Highrise account (one person, one vote per seat). Votes are final once cast and cannot be changed. Vote privacy: individual votes are not published. Only per-seat tallies are. Each voter gets a private, verifiable receipt to confirm their vote was recorded and counted; the receipt is yours alone and does not reveal your choice to others.
terms.s5.p: By self-nominating you grant Pocket Worlds a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to publish, display, translate, and process your answers to the application's open questions for the election and the Voting Advice Application (VAA). The tool maps each written answer to a position, but your confirmed positions are authoritative: you review and edit them before voting opens, and your confirmed positions are published. You are responsible for the accuracy of your submission. The full VAA methodology will be published. All candidacies are subject to review of account background and any community reports; Pocket Worlds may decline or remove a candidacy at its discretion, and the reasons will be disclosed privately to the affected candidate.
terms.s6.p: Elected terms run 6 months, max two consecutive for elected seats. Seats are personal and non-transferable: never sold, lent, or assigned. You may resign at any time. A seat left vacant mid-term stays empty until the next election. Vacancies are not backfilled during a term.
terms.s7.p: The Council operates openly: members are under no confidentiality obligation and may discuss and share Council materials publicly. Accordingly, Pocket Worlds will share with the Council only materials it is comfortable being made public. Nothing shared should be assumed secret or treated as a leak.
terms.s8.p: No harassment, hate, threats, or doxxing. No vote-buying, bribery, or exchanging anything of value for votes. No impersonation, fraud, or material misrepresentation. No sybil/multi-account voting and no snapshot manipulation. Disclose conflicts of interest. Follow Highrise/HCC community guidelines and applicable law.
terms.s9.p: One eligible account, one ballot per seat. Pocket Worlds may void votes, disqualify candidates, remove members, or bar future participation for breach, at its reasonable discretion, with reasons published where practical.
terms.s10.p: To authenticate and check eligibility we process your Discord ID, Highrise ID, Person ID, linked wallet address(es) and wallet-change history (via Discord OAuth and Highrise's internal API), plus the holdings snapshot, vote records (kept private), candidate answers (public), and voter answers (private; used to compute your own affinity, not published per-user). Candidate answers are sent to Anthropic (Claude) so the tool can map each into a position the candidate confirms. On-chain/wallet data is inherently public. See the Privacy Policy for retention and deletion-request handling.
terms.s11.p: Provided "as is." The VAA affinity score is advisory and not guaranteed accurate. Nothing here is financial, investment, tax, or legal advice, a securities offering, or a guarantee of any NFT's value. Liability is limited to the extent permitted by law; candidates indemnify Pocket Worlds for content they submit.
privacy.who.p: The HCC Player Council election is operated by Pocket Worlds ("we", "us"). This policy explains what we collect, why, who we share it with, and your choices. Data requests/questions: Highrise Discord support channel.
privacy.collect.p:
• Account & identity: via Discord OAuth, your Discord ID and the basic profile you authorize; via Highrise's internal API, your Highrise ID, Person ID, linked wallet address(es), and wallet-change history.
  • Eligibility: HCC NFT holdings and transfer history for your current primary wallet, read from public blockchains.
  • Participation: candidate answers and positions (public), voter answers (private), votes (private), and terms-acceptance records.
  • Technical: a login session cookie and basic server logs (e.g., IP, timestamps) for security.
privacy.use.p: To authenticate you; verify eligibility (3-month holding + bracket); run the VAA matching; record and tally votes and issue your private receipt; publish candidate answers/positions and aggregate results; review candidacies and enforce election integrity.
privacy.cookies.p: A single session cookie keeps you logged in after Discord OAuth. No third-party advertising or tracking cookies.
privacy.share.p:
• Anthropic (Claude): candidate answers are sent to Anthropic to map each written answer to a position the candidate then reviews and confirms. Voter data and individual votes are not sent to Anthropic.
  • Discord: for OAuth login.
  • Highrise / Pocket Worlds internal systems: identity and eligibility resolution.
  • Public blockchain explorers (Immutable/Blockscout, etc.): we query public chain data.
  • Hosting/infrastructure: to run the site and store election data.
We do not sell your personal data.
privacy.public.p: Public: candidate answers, candidate positions, and aggregate election statistics. Most election statistics (per-seat tallies, turnout, bracket breakdowns, etc.) are published on the website. Private: your individual vote (never published), your voter answers, and your vote receipt. Wallet/on-chain data is inherently public on the blockchain.
privacy.retention.p: We keep election data with no fixed deletion date. You can still ask us to delete your personal data as described below.
privacy.rights.p: You may request access to or deletion of your personal data, subject to legal and election-integrity limits, by contacting Highrise Discord support channel. Where applicable law (e.g., GDPR/CCPA) grants further rights, we honor them.
privacy.security.p: We use reasonable technical and organizational measures; no system is perfectly secure. The election algorithms and the website's structure are open-source and auditable by all users, so anyone can inspect how data is processed and how votes are counted.
privacy.children.p: The election is not directed to children, consistent with Highrise's policies.
privacy.changes.p: We may update this policy; all changes are published on the website and in Discord. Contact: Highrise Discord support channel.

guide.h2: Owning your creature, step by step
guide.lead: How to buy, sell, move, and protect your HCC NFTs, step by step. Put together with the community.
guide.what.lead: Your creature and your LAND are NFTs: items you truly own on the blockchain, not just inside an app. Here's what that means.
guide.what.c1p: An NFT is a one-of-a-kind item recorded on the blockchain. Your creature is yours to keep, wear, sell, or gift.
guide.what.c2p: HCC creatures live on the Immutable zkEVM network, a fast, low-fee blockchain built for game items.
guide.what.c3p: Your wallet, like MetaMask, is how you prove ownership and move your assets. Guard it like your house keys.
guide.what.c4p: Token Trove is the marketplace where you buy, sell, and transfer your creatures.
guide.kit.lead: Four things you'll meet again and again: your wallet, the marketplace, and the two coins you'll need.
guide.kit.c1p: Your crypto wallet. Holds your funds and creatures, and signs every action. Get it as a browser extension or mobile app.
guide.kit.c2p: The official HCC marketplace. Find the link in the Highrise Discord under official links, never from a random DM.
guide.kit.c3p: Ethereum ($ETH) is the currency you use to buy creatures.
guide.kit.c4p: IMX covers the tiny network fee ("gas") on every action. Keep a little on hand.
guide.kit.network: Creatures live on the Immutable zkEVM network. You'll switch your wallet to it when buying or moving creatures. Token Trove walks you through it each time.
guide.steps.lead: Six short guides, in the order you'll likely need them. Pick a step below. Most come with a community video to follow along.
guide.g1.h: Find Token Trove & link your wallet
guide.g1.p: Get to the official marketplace and connect MetaMask so you can see your balances and creatures.
guide.g1.s1: Open the Highrise Discord and go to the official links channel. Find the link to buy Highrise creatures. It takes you straight to Token Trove.
guide.g1.s2: Have your MetaMask wallet ready (extension or mobile app) and make sure you're logged in.
guide.g1.s3: On Token Trove, click Connect Wallet. Choose Immutable zkEVM, then pick MetaMask.
guide.g1.s4: Approve the connection in MetaMask. Token Trove now shows your balances (ETH, IMX, USDC) and your creatures under My NFTs.
guide.g2.p: Bridging moves your crypto from Ethereum mainnet to the Immutable zkEVM network where creatures live. Before bridging, you'll need a small amount of $IMX: every action on Immutable requires it as a network fee. Balances can take 20–40 minutes to appear.
guide.g2.s1: Before anything else, swap a little $ETH to $IMX in MetaMask. $IMX is the fee currency for every action on Immutable zkEVM (buying, selling, transferring). Around 0.0025 $ETH worth is plenty to start. Do this swap before bridging.
guide.g2.s2: On Token Trove, confirm you're connected and logged in, and that you can see the Bridge button. Click Bridge.
guide.g2.s3: Bridge $IMX first. Pick $IMX as the token, enter an amount (e.g. 20 $IMX), check the small fee, and confirm.
guide.g2.s4: Your wallet switches to Ethereum mainnet automatically. Confirm the two MetaMask pop-ups: the network fee, then the transfer itself.
guide.g2.s5: Now bridge your ETH the same way. This is what you'll buy creatures with. Pick ETH, enter an amount (e.g. 0.025), and confirm the single request.
guide.g2.s6: Wait roughly 20–40 minutes. When it's done, your $ETH and $IMX balances appear on Token Trove, ready to use.
guide.g2.note: Remember: $ETH buys creatures, $IMX pays the gas. You need a little $IMX for anything you do on Immutable: buying, selling, or transferring.
guide.g3.p: With funds bridged over, you're ready to shop the collection or list one of your own.
guide.g3.s1: Browse the collection and pick the creature you want. Before buying, switch your wallet to the Immutable zkEVM network: open MetaMask, select Immutable zkEVM, then refresh the page.
guide.g3.s2: Click Buy Now. Review the small network fee (this is what IMX is for) and click Confirm.
guide.g3.s3: Once the blockchain confirms, the creature is yours. Refresh your balances and check My NFTs to see it.
guide.g3.s4: To sell, open one of your creatures and click List Now. Set your price and confirm the signature request in MetaMask.
guide.g3.s5: Your creature is now listed. Anyone can buy it directly. You don't have to do anything else until it sells.
guide.g3.note: When a creature sells, a 5% creator royalty is built into the smart contract and comes out of the sale price automatically. Worth factoring into the price you set.
guide.g4.h: Transfer a creature to another wallet
guide.g4.p: Send a creature straight to another wallet, handy for moving between your own wallets or gifting.
guide.g4.s1: Open the creature you want to send and click the Transfer button, the little paper-airplane icon.
guide.g4.s2: Paste the destination wallet address. Double-check it: transfers can't be undone.
guide.g4.s3: Review the small gas fee and click Confirm. The Immutable zkEVM network confirms the transfer.
guide.g4.s4: After a few seconds, refresh My NFTs. The creature leaves your wallet and lands in the new one. A full page refresh helps if it lingers.
guide.g4.note: Always paste and verify the address yourself. There's no undo, and no one can reverse a transfer to the wrong wallet.
guide.g5.p: Connect your wallet to your Highrise account so your creatures, items, and perks show up in the app.
guide.g5.s1: Open the Highrise Discord, go to official links, and click the top one, the Highrise website. Log into your account.
guide.g5.s2: Go to your account Settings and scroll to the bottom, to Connect MetaMask Wallet. Make sure you're logged into the MetaMask wallet you want to link.
guide.g5.s3: Click Connect MetaMask Wallet. When highrise.game asks to connect, click Connect.
guide.g5.s4: Confirm the signature request. It just lets Highrise read your wallet. You're linked, and your creatures now show up in Highrise under Your Collections.
guide.g6.h: Mint LAND you bought with Deeds
guide.g6.p: Bought a parcel during an in-app LAND Deeds sale? It lives inside Highrise until you mint it onto the blockchain. Minting is what lets you sell, transfer, or trade it on OpenSea.
guide.g6.cap: Withdrawing a plot from your Highrise inventory
guide.g6.s1: Go to highrise.game and log in with the Highrise account that holds your plot. Make sure your MetaMask wallet is ready.
guide.g6.s2: Click your avatar in the top-right corner, then open Inventory. Your plot (or plots) shows up there.
guide.g6.s3: Click the specific plot you want to put on-chain, then press Withdraw.
guide.g6.s4: MetaMask pops up. Confirm and Sign the transaction. Keep a little ETH in your wallet to cover the gas fee.
guide.g6.s5: Once it confirms, your parcel is minted onto the blockchain and ready to trade, sell, or transfer on OpenSea.
guide.g6.note: Until you mint it, the plot stays tied to the Highrise account it was bought with. It can't move between accounts or wallets until it's on-chain.

gm.demo.n.browse: Start by browsing what's on sale to find the one you want. The price under each is the full, all-in amount with every fee included, so nothing gets added later.
gm.demo.n.filter: Too many to scan? Tap a rarity chip up top and the grid narrows to just those. Tap the same chip again to clear it and see everything.
gm.demo.n.open: Click any tile to open its full card. The rarity rank and traits shown there are how you judge whether the asking price is fair before you buy.
gm.demo.n.buy: Once you've decided, click the Buy now button. This only opens the checkout, so nothing leaves your wallet yet; you confirm the real amount in the next step.
gm.demo.n.check: Before your wallet even opens, the site checks your balance covers the price. If anything's short it shows a help panel, so a purchase never fails and wastes a fee.
gm.demo.n.quote: Read this quote before you agree: exactly what you send, what you get back, the fee, and how long it takes. If any number looks off, stop here, nothing has happened yet.
gm.demo.n.walletBuy: Now MetaMask opens with the real charge. Check it matches the price you just saw, then press Confirm to buy. If anything looks wrong, press Reject; rejecting always costs nothing.
gm.demo.n.walletMove: MetaMask opens showing exactly what it will move. Compare it against the quote you just saw, then press Confirm. If the numbers don't match, press Reject and start over.
gm.demo.n.walletSend: This is your last check: the right item going to the right address. Only press Confirm when both are correct, because a transfer can't be undone once it's sent.
gm.demo.n.walletConnect: MetaMask asks to connect and to add the network. Approve both. This gives the site view access and adds the network to your wallet; it never grants permission to spend or move anything.
gm.demo.n.wait: Your part is done. The network is now recording the sale on the blockchain, which usually takes a few seconds. There's nothing more for you to tap.
gm.demo.n.crossing: Coins can't jump between networks, so a bridge carries yours across. It's safe and hands-off: you can even close the page, the money is in transit, never lost.
gm.demo.n.landed: Watch the top bar: the balance just updated. That refreshed number is how you confirm the move landed, here or in any wallet app.
gm.demo.n.card: No crypto yet? Tap Buy crypto with card. It opens a normal checkout, so you can pay by card without ever opening an account on a crypto exchange.
gm.demo.n.pay: Fill it in like any online payment: card, Apple Pay or Google Pay. You're buying exactly the amount shown, priced for this purchase, nothing extra.
gm.demo.n.paid: Payment done. Your ETH takes a few minutes to arrive, and the balance in the top bar updates on its own, so there's nothing to refresh or claim.
gm.demo.n.pick: Tap the one you want to send to select it. If it's missing, it's probably listed for sale; cancel that listing first and it reappears here.
gm.demo.n.paste: Paste the recipient's address into the box, and never type it by hand. One wrong character sends the item to a stranger for good, and no one can reverse it.
gm.demo.n.checking: Hold on a moment: the site is checking this address on the blockchain before it lets you send, so a bad one gets caught early.
gm.demo.n.badaddr: See the red block? The check found a wrong character in the address. Ask the receiver to send it again and copy it fresh; never try to fix an address by eye.
gm.demo.n.retype: This time the address is copied straight from the source. Copying, never typing, is the one habit that prevents almost every lost transfer.
gm.demo.n.green: Three green checks now: the address is valid, has real on-chain activity, and can receive what you're sending. Only when all three pass does the Send button unlock.
gm.demo.n.send: The address passed every check, so tap Send. One last wallet confirmation and it's on its way.
gm.demo.n.sending: Sent. Keep the explorer link that appears: it's your public receipt, proof the transfer happened if you ever need it.
gm.demo.n.connect: To buy, sell or transfer, you first connect your wallet to the site. Find the Connect MetaMask button and click it. This link is view-only: the site can see your address and holdings, but never touches or moves your assets.
gm.demo.n.safety: Before you connect, stop and read these four habits. They take seconds, and almost every stolen wallet came from breaking one of them.
gm.demo.n.timer: The button stays locked while the timer counts down. That's on purpose: use those few seconds to actually read the rules above before you continue.
gm.demo.n.network: Approve once and MetaMask saves the network your items live on. It's a one-time step; your wallet won't ask about this network again.
gm.demo.n.balances: You're in. The top bar now reads your address and balances straight from the blockchain. Whenever a wallet app looks odd, trust these numbers, they're the source of truth.
gm.demo.n.sign: This is a signature, not a payment. Signing only proves the wallet is yours; it costs nothing, moves nothing, and your keys never leave MetaMask, so it's safe to approve.
gm.demo.n.applink: On highrise.game, open Settings and scroll to Connect MetaMask Wallet near the bottom. First make sure you're logged into the Highrise account you want your items on.
gm.demo.n.sold: The sale settled by itself: the buyer's payment is already in your wallet. There's nothing to claim and no deadline, so whatever you do next is on your own time.
gm.demo.n.cashguide: When you want it as spendable money, tap Cash out in the top bar. It walks you through the safe route step by step, so just follow along.
gm.demo.n.readwarn: Read this warning before anything else. Sending to an exchange the wrong way loses the money for good, and that's exactly what these steps prevent.
gm.demo.n.approve: MetaMask will ask twice, and that's normal. The first approves exactly this amount and nothing more; the second actually moves it. Read each and only Confirm when it looks right.
gm.demo.n.swap: Tap Get IMX gas. It turns a couple of dollars of your ETH into IMX, the coin that pays the small network fee on every action you take here.
gm.demo.n.unwrap: Tap Unwrap to ETH. It's the same coin and the same amount; unwrapping only removes the wrapped label that some exchanges won't accept.

gm.cash.h: Turn your sale into money in your bank
gm.cash.p: You sold, congratulations! Your ETH sits safely in your own wallet until you move it. The whole cash-out happens on this page, and the walkthrough below shows every tap before you make it.
gm.cash.calm1p: Your ETH never passes through us or anyone else. It moves between networks inside the same wallet, same address, and only you can approve each step.
gm.cash.calm2p: The move usually lands in a few minutes and runs on its own. Close the page if you like. The tracker keeps going and picks up right where it was.
gm.cash.calm3p: Unsure at any step? Stop. Nothing happens without your confirmation. Ask in the Highrise Discord and a real person will help.
gm.cash.cr.where: Creature sales pay you in ETH on Immutable zkEVM. We move it to Ethereum for you on this page.
gm.cash.cr.note: Don't send this ETH straight from Immutable zkEVM to an exchange. Most exchanges only accept ETH on Ethereum. That's what the Cash out button does: it moves your ETH to Ethereum first.
gm.cash.cr.note2: After it lands: open MetaMask, switch the network picker to Ethereum, and your ETH is right there (the site's "Show it in MetaMask" button does the switch for you). Where to sell it, and what each option costs, is just below.
gm.cash.la.where: LAND sales pay you in WETH on Ethereum. One tap unwraps it to plain ETH, no bridging needed.
gm.cash.la.note: WETH ("wrapped ETH") is worth exactly the same as ETH. It's just a different token, and none of the places below will credit a WETH deposit. The unwrap is a 1:1 swap back to plain ETH that costs only gas. After that, pick where to sell it below.
gm.paid.lead: Your ETH is on Ethereum now, in your own wallet, and it's safe there for as long as you like. When you want it as money in your bank, here are the four places people go. Open any of them for the full picture.
gm.paid.pick1.p: On a computer, use MetaMask's own sell page. It's the only one here with no deposit address to copy and no network to choose, and those are the two steps where people lose the whole sale. On a phone, open the MetaMask app and use its Sell tab instead.
gm.paid.pick2.p: Four figures or more? An exchange costs a fraction of the fee and the gap is worth the extra steps. Finish the ID checks and link your bank before you send any ETH, or your money sits waiting on a document review.
gm.paid.pick3.p: Where you live changes the answer more than anything else on this page. Turkey, the UK and a few US states rule options out completely, and sanctions rule out whole countries. Pick your country further down and this page tells you what's left.
gm.paid.mm.what: One page inside MetaMask that asks several payment companies for a price at the same time. You pick the best offer, do that company's ID check on their site, then send the ETH. No deposit address to paste, and no network to pick.
gm.paid.mm.cost: The most you'll pay of the four. Measured across eleven countries and payment methods in August 2026, the all-in cost ran from 1% to over 10%. The offers differ a lot, so read the whole list rather than taking the first one.
gm.paid.mm.acct: No account with us, and none with MetaMask. The company behind the offer you pick runs its own ID check, and you finish that before you send anything.
gm.paid.mm.time: Minutes to a card. Instant on Brazilian Pix and UK Faster Payments. One to five days on a US or European bank transfer.
gm.paid.mm.catch: It only works in a browser on a computer. On a phone or tablet it shows an app advert instead, which looks broken but isn't. Small sales are punished hard: 0.005 ETH came back worth about 67% of its market value, where 0.05 ETH came back at 93%. Once you send, the payment company holds your money until it reaches you.
gm.paid.cb.kind: Exchange. Send ETH in, sell it, withdraw cash.
gm.paid.cb.what: The broadest coverage of the three, and the one members here name most often.
gm.paid.cb.cost: Much less than a sell tool, but it depends which screen you use. The one-tap Buy and Sell tile costs several times the Advanced order book for exactly the same trade. Check your own rate on its fee page before you sell.
gm.paid.cb.acct: Yours to open, with ID checks. Do those and link your bank before you send anything.
gm.paid.cb.time: Minutes for the deposit to land, then your bank's own speed. Instant on UK Faster Payments and Brazilian Pix, one to three working days on a US transfer.
gm.paid.cb.catch: No Turkish lira, and it won't take WETH. It will try to recover a deposit sent on the wrong network, but only on Ethereum, Polygon and BNB Chain, and it charges 5% of whatever is above $100. Nothing sent from Immutable zkEVM is recoverable anywhere.
gm.paid.kr.kind: Exchange. The clearest about what it charges.
gm.paid.kr.what: The same shape as Coinbase, with unusually plain published fees and strong Brazilian Pix in both directions.
gm.paid.kr.cost: Its Pro order book was 0.40% to place a price and 0.80% to take one when we checked in August 2026. The one-tap instant trade is 1%, or 1.5% on a custom order, plus a spread it doesn't publish. Cashing out costs nothing on a US transfer, 1 euro on SEPA, 1.95 pounds on Faster Payments and 0.50% on Brazilian Pix.
gm.paid.kr.acct: Yours to open, with ID checks.
gm.paid.kr.time: Minutes for the deposit. Instant SEPA and Brazilian Pix, near-instant UK Faster Payments, one to two days on a US transfer.
gm.paid.kr.catch: It says in writing that anything sent to the wrong deposit address won't be credited and won't be returned, and every token there has its own address even though they all start with 0x. No Turkish lira, and it doesn't serve Maine, New York or Japan.
gm.paid.bn.kind: Exchange. The cheapest, if you can use it.
gm.paid.bn.what: The lowest trading fee of the three by a wide margin. The catch is which of its sites you're allowed to use.
gm.paid.bn.cost: 0.10% on the spot order book, or 0.075% if you pay the fee in BNB. That price is on the order book screen, not the one-tap convert screen.
gm.paid.bn.acct: Yours to open, on the right site for your country. binance.com for most of the world, binance.us in the United States, binance.tr for Turkish lira. ID checks don't carry across them, so each one is a fresh signup.
gm.paid.bn.time: Minutes for the deposit, then one to three working days on a European transfer.
gm.paid.bn.catch: binance.com doesn't serve the United States at all, and Binance.US skips sixteen states, two of which take crypto but not dollars. It hasn't accepted a new UK customer since 16 October 2023, and that was still true on 29 August 2026.

gm.paid.rule1.t: Send ETH, on Ethereum, and nothing else
gm.paid.rule1.p: Every exchange here takes ETH on Ethereum. None of them takes anything on Immutable zkEVM, and a deposit sent that way is gone for good. Holding WETH from a LAND sale? Unwrap it to plain ETH first, because none of these will credit WETH, MetaMask Sell included. Paste the deposit address, check its first six and last six characters against the exchange's own screen, then send a small test before the rest.
gm.paid.rule2.p: Start at the last dot before the first slash. The two parts there have to be the real name: metamask.io, coinbase.com, kraken.com, binance.com. Anything in front of that means nothing, which is exactly how portfolio.metamask.en-eu.io works. That one is a real fake on MetaMask's own blocklist and it reads fine left to right. Nobody from HCC, Highrise, MetaMask or any exchange will ever ask you for your twelve words.
gm.paid.go.check: After it opens, check your address bar ends in the bold part.
gm.paid.usdt.intro: Club refunds are paid in USDT on Ethereum, sent to the wallet that returned the assets. That's good news: USDT is a dollar coin, so 210 USDT is worth about 210 dollars today, next week and next month. Your refund doesn't ride the crypto market while you decide, there's no clock on selling it, and every route above takes it at close to face value. Here's the trip, step by step.
gm.paid.usdt.s1: Switch MetaMask to Ethereum. That's the network refunds arrive on, and yours shows as a USDT balance under your tokens, usually within five business days of your transfer. Got USDT from somewhere else instead? Check the network picker first: coins on Tron, Solana or another network take a different road, and these steps fit Ethereum only.
gm.paid.usdt.s2: Ignore copycat tokens. Scammers watch these payouts and send a fake coin also named "USDT" minutes after the real one, so a block explorer may show your refund twice. The balance MetaMask shows on its own is the real one. They strike again the moment you send: a fake token fakes a second send from your wallet to an address that starts and ends like the real one. Never open a website a strange token points you to, never swap or approve a coin you didn't expect, and never copy an address from your history.
gm.paid.usdt.s3: Keep a little ETH in the same wallet. Moving USDT costs a small fee paid in ETH, so with zero ETH the coins can't move at all. A few dollars' worth is plenty.
gm.paid.usdt.s4: The easy route is the same sell page as for ETH: portfolio.metamask.io/sell, on a computer. Pick USDT as the coin to sell and compare the offers. It quoted mainnet USDT when we checked on 30 August 2026, at about 3% under face value.
gm.paid.usdt.s5: The cheap route is an exchange, and all three above take USDT. On the deposit screen pick USDT first, then the network, and it must say Ethereum or ERC-20 to match your wallet. Kraken alone offers eighteen networks for USDT, which is exactly how picking by eye loses the coins. Send a small test before the rest, and paste the address fresh from the exchange for the rest. Your history is where the fakes live.
gm.paid.usdt.s6: Once it lands, sell the USDT for your currency (near 1:1, since it's a dollar coin) and withdraw to your bank the way the cards above describe.

gm.get.cex.name: An exchange
gm.get.cex.what: Buy ETH on an exchange, then withdraw it to your own wallet. Come back to Add funds, pick where it landed, and the site brings it to Immutable zkEVM in about seven seconds.
gm.get.cex.cost: Well under 1% all in: a fraction of a percent to trade, a small withdrawal fee (about 17 cents on Binance in August 2026), and about a cent for the move across from Ethereum.
gm.get.cex.acct: An account and an ID check at the exchange, plus a way to pay. Finish both before you buy, or your money waits on a document review.
gm.get.cex.time: Ten minutes or so across three steps, once the account exists. The move to Immutable zkEVM takes seconds.
gm.get.cex.catch: Withdraw on Ethereum unless its network fee is spiking. Base, Arbitrum and OP Mainnet all work too, and cost less to withdraw to, but the move across costs about 40 cents more from there.
gm.get.rule1.t: Withdraw on a network we can pick up
gm.get.rule1.p: Checked in August 2026 against their own systems: Coinbase sends ETH on Arbitrum, Base, Ethereum, Optimism, Polygon and Unichain. Binance sends it on nine networks. Add funds picks up Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum and OP Mainnet, so choose one of those, paste your own wallet address, and send a small test before the rest.

guide.safe.lead: Your creatures and LAND are worth real money, and on-chain ownership is final. Here are the habits that keep them safe, the scams to know, and what to do if you slip. We keep this page updated, so it's worth a bookmark.
guide.safe.habits.h2: The basics that keep you safe
guide.safe.c1p: Your seed phrase is the 12 random words shown once when you created your wallet. It's the master key: whoever has it controls your wallet completely. No one, not Highrise and not support, will ever need it.
guide.safe.c2p: Only use links from the Highrise Discord's official links channel. Never trust marketplace or wallet links sent via DMs, social media comments, or sites you didn't find yourself.
guide.safe.c3p: Before any transfer, paste and re-read the destination address. Transfers are permanent and can't be reversed.
guide.safe.c4p: Every action on Immutable needs a tiny $IMX fee. Keep a small balance so you're never stuck mid-transaction.
guide.safe.c6p: Every wallet popup spends or approves something. Slow down and read what it does. Sites asking you to "validate", "sync" or "migrate" your wallet are scams. No real app needs that.
guide.safe.c7p: Your Creatures live on the Immutable zkEVM network. Only transfer them to wallets on that same network, and don't use a marketplace's "withdraw" option to move a Creature off it unless you're certain what it does. Send to the wrong network and it's gone for good.
guide.safe.c8p: Gen 1 Creatures only trade on Token Trove. Any "Highrise Creature" or "Highrise Creature Club" collection on OpenSea is a fake. Gen 1 isn't listed there. Only LAND and Gen 2 are on OpenSea. Reach every marketplace through the official Discord links.
guide.safe.hacked.p: Clicked a bad link or signed something suspicious? Act fast: move your Creatures and funds to a fresh wallet first, then revoke old approvals from the compromised one, and tell the team in the public Discord so others get warned. Speed matters more than embarrassment. Everyone has a close call eventually.
guide.safe.c5p: Real staff won't DM you first asking for wallet access, payments, or your phrase. When in doubt, ask in the public Discord.
guide.safe.alert: HCC staff and support will never message you first. If anyone DMs you claiming to be from the team and asks for wallet access, your seed phrase, or any payment, it's a scam. Ask publicly in the Highrise Discord instead.

guide.scam.h2: Know the tricks before they find you
guide.scam.lead: Scammers target Creature and LAND holders because the assets are worth real money. Here's the full playbook they run, the red flags that give it away, and what to do if you slip. We add new scams as they show up, so it's worth a bookmark.
guide.scam.rule.p: Never type your 12-word seed phrase anywhere, and never approve a wallet request you don't fully understand. Nearly every drained wallet starts the moment one of those two slips.
guide.scam.tactics.lead: Tap any card for how the trick works, the red flags, and exactly what to do. These are the ones actually hitting Highrise holders.
guide.scam.t1.s: A "free" item you never bought lands in your wallet
guide.scam.t1.how: Scammers send an unsolicited NFT (often a lookalike like a fake "Highrise Estate") straight to your wallet. Its image, name or description carries a link to "claim", "unlock" or "sell" it. That link leads to a drainer site that asks you to connect and sign, and the signature hands over your real assets. Just receiving it is harmless. Interacting with it is the trap.
guide.scam.t1.f1: An item appears that you never bought or claimed.
guide.scam.t1.f2: Its details push you to visit a site to "claim" or "redeem" value.
guide.scam.t1.d1: Don't click anything on it. Don't try to sell, transfer or "claim" it.
guide.scam.t1.d2: Hide it in your wallet or marketplace and carry on. It can't hurt you sitting there.
guide.scam.t2.how: A site tells you to sign to "connect", "verify" or "claim". The request is actually a token approval or a blanket "set approval for all" that lets the scammer move your Creatures or funds whenever they like. It feels routine, so people click through without reading.
guide.scam.t2.f1: A signature request you didn't start, or that mentions "approve", "permit" or "set approval for all".
guide.scam.t2.f2: The site rushes you or says signing is "just to log in".
guide.scam.t2.d1: Read every wallet popup. If you can't explain what it approves, reject it.
guide.scam.t2.d2: Review and revoke old approvals now and then with a tool like revoke.cash.
guide.scam.t3.how: Someone copies a team member's name and avatar and DMs you offering to "fix" a problem or "verify" your wallet. They send you to a phishing site or a fake ticket bot. Real staff and support never message you first.
guide.scam.t3.f1: An unprompted DM claiming to be staff, support or a "helper".
guide.scam.t3.f2: Pressure to act fast, move to another app, or open a link.
guide.scam.t3.d1: Assume any first-contact DM is a scam. Don't reply, don't click.
guide.scam.t3.d2: Ask your question in the public Highrise Discord instead.
guide.scam.t4.s: A form asks for your 12 words
guide.scam.t4.how: A site or DM claims your wallet needs to be "validated", "synced", "migrated" or "restored", then shows a box to type your 12-word seed phrase. Anyone who gets those words owns your wallet forever. No real app or person ever needs them.
guide.scam.t4.f1: Any request to enter, confirm or "back up" your seed phrase online.
guide.scam.t4.f2: Words like validate, sync, migrate or restore attached to your wallet.
guide.scam.t4.d1: Never type your seed phrase anywhere. Close the page immediately.
guide.scam.t4.d2: Keep it offline only. MetaMask never asks for it after setup.
guide.scam.t5.s: A convincing clone of the real thing
guide.scam.t5.how: Scammers spin up a fake "Highrise Creature" collection on OpenSea, or a phishing clone of Token Trove at a near-identical web address. You connect your wallet expecting the real site and sign a drainer request. Gen 1 Creatures only trade on Token Trove. Any Gen 1 "Highrise Creature" collection on OpenSea is fake.
guide.scam.t5.f1: A web address with an extra letter, dash or odd ending you don't recognize.
guide.scam.t5.f2: A "Highrise Creature" Gen 1 listing anywhere but Token Trove.
guide.scam.t5.d1: Reach every marketplace through the official links in the Highrise Discord.
guide.scam.t5.d2: Check the exact address before connecting. See the Links tab for the real ones.
guide.scam.t6.how: A post or DM says you won a prize, a whitelist spot, or a limited free mint. To "claim" it you connect your wallet and sign. The claim is a drainer, or the "small gas fee" is the theft itself. Urgency and a countdown are the bait.
guide.scam.t6.f1: A win or free mint you never signed up for, with a ticking timer.
guide.scam.t6.f2: "Just connect and sign to claim" or "pay a small fee to release it".
guide.scam.t6.d1: Treat every surprise prize as fake until confirmed in an official channel.
guide.scam.t6.d2: Real HCC drops come through official Highrise channels, never a random DM.
guide.scam.t7.s: A hacked friend or fake "verify" bot
guide.scam.t7.how: A hacked friend's account sends you a link, or a fake bot tells you to "re-verify" by scanning a QR code or authorizing an app. Scanning a Discord login QR from a stranger hands them your account. Malicious links can also install software that reads your wallet.
guide.scam.t7.f1: A "verify", "re-verify" or QR-scan prompt from a DM or unknown bot.
guide.scam.t7.f2: A friend suddenly sharing a link, a giveaway, or a "free Nitro" offer.
guide.scam.t7.d1: Never scan a login QR you didn't generate yourself. Turn on 2FA.
guide.scam.t7.d2: If a friend sends something odd, confirm with them another way first.
guide.scam.t8.s: A lookalike address in your history
guide.scam.t8.how: Scammers send tiny transactions from an address that starts and ends with the same characters as one you use. Later, you copy the address from your history to send funds, grab the lookalike by mistake, and the money goes to them. Transfers can't be reversed.
guide.scam.t8.f1: Tiny unexpected transfers from an address that looks familiar.
guide.scam.t8.f2: Relying on your transaction history to copy a "known" address.
guide.scam.t8.d1: Check the full address, not just the first and last few characters.
guide.scam.t8.d2: Send a tiny test amount first, or use a saved, verified address book.
guide.scam.t9.s: Your refund seems to arrive twice
guide.scam.t9.how: The club's refund program pays in real USDT on Ethereum. Scammers watch those payouts on-chain and, minutes later, send the same wallets a worthless copy: a token with the same name and the same amount. On a block explorer the two look identical, so it reads like a second refund. The copy exists to make you touch it. Trying to sell, swap or "claim" it leads to a site whose approval hands your wallet over. We've watched this shadow real refund payouts, about fifteen minutes behind each one.
guide.scam.t9.how2: There's a second act. The moment you send real USDT anywhere, even a one-dollar test to an exchange, a fake token fakes a send from your wallet to an address that starts and ends like the real one. Your history now shows two sends. Copy the wrong one for the rest and it's gone for good. We watched this hit a refunded member twelve seconds after their test.
guide.scam.t9.f1: Your refund shows twice on a block explorer, but MetaMask lists it once.
guide.scam.t9.f2: A "USDT" balance pushes you toward a website, or a swap you didn't start.
guide.scam.t9.f3: Right after you send USDT, a second send you never made appears in your history, to an address that starts and ends like the real one.
guide.scam.t9.d1: Trust the balance MetaMask shows on its own. That's the real USDT, and the double is the fake.
guide.scam.t9.d2: Don't sell, swap or approve the copy. It can't hurt you sitting there. Then cash out the real one with the USDT steps in the Marketplace guide.
guide.scam.t9.d3: When you send the rest, don't copy the address from your history. Paste it fresh from the exchange's deposit screen and check the whole thing, middle included.
guide.scam.flow.h2: How an airdrop empties a wallet
guide.scam.flow.lead: The exact chain of events behind the fake-NFT trick, so you can spot where to stop it. The safe move is to break the chain at step one.
guide.scam.flow.s1p: An NFT you never bought shows up in your wallet. It's designed to look valuable and to make you curious.
guide.scam.flow.s2h: It lures you to a site
guide.scam.flow.s2p: Its name or description carries a link to "claim", "sell" or "unlock" it. The link opens a drainer dressed up as a real marketplace.
guide.scam.flow.s3p: The site asks you to connect and approve a request. It looks routine, but the signature grants access to your real assets.
guide.scam.flow.s4p: With that approval, the scammer moves out your Creatures and funds. On-chain transfers are final, so there's no undo.
guide.scam.flow.note: Break the chain at step one: never interact with an item you didn't buy. Receiving it is harmless. Clicking is the trap.
guide.scam.spot.lead: Here's a real-style DM. Tap every part that looks like a red flag. See how many you catch.
guide.scam.spot.dm.name: Hlghrise Support
guide.scam.spot.dm.l1: Hey! This is the official Highrise team.
guide.scam.spot.dm.l2: We noticed suspicious activity on your wallet and need to secure it right away.
guide.scam.spot.dm.l3a: Please verify your wallet here within
guide.scam.spot.dm.l4: Have your 12-word secret phrase ready to confirm ownership.
guide.scam.spot.tip.name: Misspelled name (a capital I posing as an l) and a fake "MOD" badge. Impostors copy real names with tiny changes.
guide.scam.spot.tip.first: Real staff never DM you first about your wallet. First contact is the tell.
guide.scam.spot.tip.urgency: A countdown is pure pressure. Urgency is designed to stop you thinking.
guide.scam.spot.tip.link: A lookalike address that isn't the official site. Never connect a wallet through a DM link.
guide.scam.spot.tip.seed: No one legitimate ever needs your 12-word secret phrase. This alone is a guaranteed scam.
guide.scam.spot.hint: Each flag you find is explained here.
guide.scam.spot.win: Nice. That instinct, treating surprises as guilty until proven safe, is what keeps your wallet yours.
guide.scam.check.lead: Tick these off once and they'll stick. Your progress is saved on this device.
guide.scam.check.c1: My seed phrase lives offline only. I've never typed it into a website.
guide.scam.check.c2: I only reach marketplaces through the official Highrise Discord links.
guide.scam.check.c3: I read every wallet popup before I sign, and reject anything I can't explain.
guide.scam.check.c4: I ignore unsolicited DMs claiming to be staff or support.
guide.scam.check.c5: I never interact with NFTs I didn't buy. I just hide them.
guide.scam.check.c6: I have 2FA on Discord and I've reviewed my wallet's token approvals.
guide.scam.check.done: You're all set. Come back any time to refresh.
guide.scam.er.lead: Clicked a bad link or signed something wrong? Move fast. Speed matters far more than embarrassment, and everyone has a close call eventually.
guide.scam.er.s1h: Disconnect and go offline from it
guide.scam.er.s1p: Close the site, disconnect your wallet from it, and stop signing anything. Don't approve one more request "to fix it".
guide.scam.er.s2h: Move your assets to a safe wallet
guide.scam.er.s2p: If you still have access, send your Creatures, LAND and funds to a fresh wallet whose seed phrase has never touched a website. Do the most valuable first.
guide.scam.er.s3p: From the compromised wallet, revoke token and collection approvals with a tool like revoke.cash. This cuts off the access the signature gave away.
guide.scam.er.s4p: Change passwords and turn on 2FA for Discord and your email. If a device feels compromised, run a malware scan before you sign anything again.
guide.scam.er.s5p: Tell the team in the public Highrise Discord with what happened and any links or addresses involved. Your report protects the next holder.
guide.scam.er.note: A compromised seed phrase can't be made safe again. Once assets are on a fresh wallet, treat the old one as burned and stop using it.
guide.scam.report.p: Spotted a fake site, a scam DM or a suspicious airdrop? Post it in the Highrise Discord so the team can warn everyone. Members watching out for each other is our best defense.

term.creature-club.p: The members' club built around 11,111 Creature avatars and the LAND parcels sold alongside them.
term.creature-club.b: Highrise Creature Club, HCC for short, is a members' club inside Highrise. Membership follows ownership rather than a subscription: a wallet holding a Creature or a LAND parcel is a member, and the perks, the coins, the member drops and the Council vote all follow from that. The club is run by Pocket Worlds, which also runs Highrise itself.
term.creature-club.use: The site uses club for the whole thing, Creature Club for the collection side of it, and Council for the elected body. HCC is the short form, and it prefixes the names of many of the club's older items in the archive.
term.creature-club.f2: Anyone holding a Creature or a LAND parcel
term.creature-club.h1: The first Creatures are minted, 11,111 of them, and the club opens with them.
term.creature-club.h2: LAND goes on sale as a second collectible, in Standard and Premium tiers.
term.creature-club.h3: LAND is folded into the club. Land Tokens become Creature Coins and LAND owners get Creature Club benefits.
term.creature-club.h4: A delivery reset: an artist put permanently on Gen 1 and Gen 2, updates every two weeks, monthly store refreshes, quarterly drops.
term.creature-club.h6: ItsVini takes over as project lead.
term.creature.p: One of the 11,111 avatars the club was built on, held as an NFT and wearable in Highrise.
term.creature.b: A Creature is a computer-generated avatar assembled from thirteen trait slots, minted in November 2021 and recorded on Immutable zkEVM. Each one is owned outright by a wallet rather than by a Highrise account, so it can be worn, sold or moved without the club taking part. Ten Creatures are drawn as characters rather than assembled, and 33 carry no traits at all.
term.creature.use: Creature means the Gen 1 avatar throughout the site. The number in a Creature's name, such as 3379, is how holders refer to one and how its page is addressed; the 39-digit token id is the chain's own name for the same thing.
term.creature.h1: The collection mints on Immutable StarkEx.
term.creature.h2: The collection moves to Immutable zkEVM, which is where it is traded today. The 39-digit token ids are left over from the move.
term.creature.h3: Creatures become tradable on this site.
term.gen-2.p: The second generation owed to holders: a Creature for every LAND parcel, a pet for every Gen 1 Creature.
term.gen-2.b: Gen 2 is an entitlement rather than a sale. It was promised when LAND was sold, and it has two halves: every LAND parcel is owed its own Creature, and every Gen 1 Creature is owed a pet. Production restarted in June 2026 with an update every two weeks, and the build order was revised in August 2026 to put the pets first.
term.gen-2.use: Gen 2 is not a drop and not a store release. Drops and store items are perks that ship alongside it and are never a substitute for it. The Roadmap tab tracks the pet sets and the Creature work as two separate boards.
term.gen-2.note: Gen 2 ships as a whole rather than parcel by parcel. The fullest public answer on what a holder actually receives is the Gen 2 Explained page, written from the project lead's own answers of 22 August 2026.
term.gen-2.f2: Every LAND parcel and every Gen 1 Creature
