term.land.p: The club's virtual parcels of the Highrise universe, held as NFTs on Ethereum mainnet.
term.land.b: LAND went on sale in 2022 as a second collectible, in two tiers, Standard and Premium. It was sold as custom, monetizable corners of Highrise; that plan was wound down in 2023 and LAND owners were brought into Creature Club benefits instead. A LAND owner is a full member: daily Creature Coins, room capacity boosts, every drop and giveaway, and a Council vote.
term.land.use: LAND in capitals means the collectible. Parcel and plot mean one square of it. Estate means several parcels locked into one token. LAND trades on Ethereum mainnet through OpenSea's Seaport contracts, which is why its fees look nothing like a Creature's.
term.land.h1: LAND goes on sale in Standard and Premium tiers, with Land Tokens, room capacity boosts, an exclusive shop and slime pets.
term.land.h2: The custom monetizable plan is wound down. Land Tokens convert to Creature Coins, pets stay with their owners, and Premium LAND mirrors higher-tier Creature benefits at three times the rate.
term.land.h3: The merge ships in practice: Discord access, Highrise+ eligibility and Creature Coins reach LAND owners.
term.land.h4: LAND becomes tradable on this site.
term.parcel.b: A parcel is the unit LAND is counted in. One parcel is one token on Ethereum mainnet unless it has been locked into an estate, in which case the estate contract holds it and the owner holds the estate.
term.parcel.use: Parcel and plot are used interchangeably across the site and in the Discord. Holder counts on the Holders tab count parcels, not estates.
term.estate.p: Several LAND parcels locked into a single token.
term.estate.b: Minting an estate moves its parcels into the estate contract and returns one NFT in their place, so on-chain the contract holds the land and the wallet holds the estate. The estate can then be traded as one item.
term.estate.use: An estate is not a parcel and is never counted as one. The Holders tab shows estates separately for that reason.
term.estate.note: Estate parcel counts over-report, and the club has left them that way on purpose. An estate can end up holding fewer parcels than it was minted with, and neither the mint record nor the contract's own list shrinks to match: one estate minted with 144 holds 57 today and both records still read 144. The site shows the minted figure and says so here rather than guessing at a correction.
term.estate.f3: The parcels it was minted with
term.premium-land.p: The higher of LAND's two tiers, sold above Standard.
term.premium-land.b: Premium parcels earn Creature Coins at three times the Standard rate, and the Gen 2 Creatures owed to them are exclusive to the tier. The tier was fixed at the sale and does not change with what the parcel is used for.
term.premium-land.use: Premium is a sale tier, not a rarity rank. The marketplace shows it as a tier chip on a parcel; the Perks page lists what it earns.
term.premium-land.note: A parcel's rarity tier is the tier it sold at. It says nothing about the land itself, and it does not line up with the rarity scales used for items or for Creatures.
term.premium-land.f2: The tier the parcel was sold at
term.premium-land.f3: Creature Coins at three times the Standard rate
term.premium-land.h1: LAND sells in two tiers, Standard and Premium.
term.premium-land.h2: Premium starts mirroring higher-tier Creature benefits at three times the Standard rate.
term.deed.p: The voucher a LAND sale issued, redeemable for the parcel itself.
term.deed.b: A deed stands in for a parcel until it is minted. Minting exchanges the deed for the parcel, once, in a transaction signed from the holder's own wallet. Until then the deed is what the wallet holds and what the marketplace sees.
term.deed.use: Deed appears in the LAND walkthrough and wherever a wallet's holdings are shown. An unminted deed is not yet a parcel, so it does not appear in parcel counts.
term.deed.f2: Redeemed by minting, once per deed
term.deed.h1: Deeds are issued by the LAND sale.
term.pet.p: A companion given to members, eleven of them so far.
term.pet.b: Pets have been handed out through club giveaways since July 2023, usually announced in the Discord. They are separate from the Gen 2 pets, which are owed to every Gen 1 Creature rather than given away.
term.pet.use: Pet covers both the giveaway companions in the archive and the Gen 2 pets in production. The Roadmap tab keeps the two apart.
term.pet.h2: Eleven pets have been given away in total.
term.slime.p: The pet that came with a LAND parcel, with traits and a rarity rank of its own.
term.slime.b: Slimes were part of the LAND sale and stayed with their owners when the LAND plan was wound down in 2023. The Gen 2 pets owed to Gen 1 Creatures are slimes too, planned as five sets from Sushi to Elemental.
term.slime.use: Slime means the LAND pet. It is also the shape the Gen 2 pets take, which is why the pet roadmap counts slime sets rather than pet types.
term.slime.f2: LAND parcels, and the Gen 2 pets in production
term.slime.h1: Slimes ship with the LAND sale.
term.slime.h2: Pets stay with their owners when the LAND plan is wound down.
term.slime.h3: Five Gen 2 slime sets get their own roadmap board.
term.creature-coins.p: The club's currency, earned every day by holding.
term.creature-coins.b: Coins accrue daily to Creature and LAND holders, with Premium LAND earning at three times the Standard rate. They were called Land Tokens until 2023, when LAND joined the club and the balances converted. Coins are what the Creature Store and grabs are priced in.
term.creature-coins.use: Coins are a spending balance, not an asset. They do not appear on-chain and they are not an NFT. The Perks page shows the daily rates.
term.creature-coins.note: Coins cannot be bought, sold or traded. The Council settled that at its second meeting on 16 July 2026: coins come from holding, or not at all. Everything coins buy is holder only for the same reason.
term.creature-coins.f3: Not tradable, by Council decision of 16 July 2026
term.creature-coins.h1: Land Tokens accrue to LAND owners.
term.creature-coins.h2: Land Tokens convert to Creature Coins as LAND joins the club.
term.creature-coins.h3: The Council settles that coins stay untradable.
term.holder.p: Anyone whose wallet holds a Creature or a LAND parcel.
term.holder.b: Holding is the club's only membership test. It unlocks the perks, the daily coins, the member drops and the right to vote. The site reads holdings straight from the two contracts rather than from any list of its own, so membership follows a sale within minutes.
term.holder.use: Holder counts on the Holders tab count wallets, not people: one person may hold several wallets, and one wallet may hold hundreds of assets. Council voting adds a further test, three months of continuous holding.
term.holder.f1: One Creature or one LAND parcel is enough
term.holder.f2: Read from the Creature and LAND contracts
term.holder.f3: Perks, coins, drops, giveaways and the Council vote
term.holder.h1: Any wallet's holdings become searchable on the site.
term.holder-profile.p: A public page a holder can switch on to show what that wallet holds.
term.holder-profile.b: Profiles are opt-in and off by default. Switching one on publishes a page at a fixed address so a buyer can see who they are dealing with; switching it off deletes the page and its record outright. It is the one place on the site where a wallet is shown next to an identity, and only because its owner asked for it.
term.holder-profile.use: A profile is linked from the marketplace next to a seller. Nothing appears until the holder turns it on.
term.release.p: Any batch of items the club has put out, whatever the occasion.
term.release.b: Release is the archive's umbrella word. Each one carries a date, a kind, the items in it and how many copies were made. The archive sorts them oldest to newest and is the site's record of everything the club has shipped.
term.release.use: A release is not automatically a drop. The archive files each one under one of eight kinds: drop, grab, store, event, competition, giveaway, collab and other.
term.release.f2: Eight kinds: drop, grab, store, event, competition, giveaway, collab and other
term.release.h1: The whole archive is published on the Collections tab.
term.drop.p: A themed set of items released to members, with art built around one idea.
term.drop.b: Drops are the club's member perk: a set of items with a theme, released to holders rather than sold for coins. Since the December 2025 reset the club has committed to a drop each quarter.
term.drop.use: A drop is not a store release. The store is where coins are spent; a drop is what membership pays. The archive keeps them apart deliberately.
term.drop.f2: A member perk, not bought with coins
term.drop.h1: The club commits to a drop each quarter.
term.grab.p: A spin for a random item out of a set, paid for with Creature Coins.
term.grab.b: A grab is the club's version of a gacha pull: a coin price, a set of possible items and a random result. Grabs are holder only, and the items in one are recorded in the archive like any other release.
term.grab.use: Grab is used as a noun for the release and as a verb for the spin. What comes out is random; what goes in is coins, which cannot be bought.
term.creature-store.p: The club's shop, where Creature Coins buy items nothing else can.
term.creature-store.b: The store is the club's coin sink: items priced in Creature Coins and available nowhere else. Since the December 2025 reset it has been refreshed monthly.
term.creature-store.use: Store means the club's own shop only. A Highrise shop release is not a store release and the archive does not file it as one.
term.creature-store.note: A drop and a store release are not the same thing. A drop is a member perk; the store is what coins are for. Keeping the two apart is the point of both.
term.creature-store.h1: The club commits to a monthly store refresh.
term.giveaway.p: Items handed to members for nothing, usually through the club's Discord.
term.giveaway.b: Giveaways cost neither coins nor money. Most were announced and awarded in the Discord, which is why their dates in the archive come from the giveaway posts themselves. All eleven club pets were given away this way.
term.giveaway.use: A giveaway is not a drop: a drop reaches every holder, a giveaway reaches whoever entered or was picked.
term.event-collab.p: The archive's three other kinds of release.
term.event-collab.b: An event ships around a moment, such as a holiday or a launch. A collab is made with someone outside the club. A competition rewards what members made. All three are recorded in the archive with the same fields as a drop.
term.event-collab.use: These kinds exist so the archive can be honest about how something reached holders rather than calling everything a drop.
term.announced.p: The badge on an archive release that got its own post in the announcements channel.
term.announced.b: The badge records that a release was posted in the club's Discord announcements channel, and links the archive entry to that post. The Announcements tab mirrors the same channel on this site.
term.announced.use: The badge is a fact about the record, not about the release. It is shown as a chip on the release page and as a filter in the archive.
term.announced.note: Half the archive predates the announcements channel. A missing badge means there was no post, not that there was no release.
term.announced.h1: The Announcements tab starts mirroring the channel.
term.approx-date.p: A release date worked out from when its items were made rather than from a post.
term.approx-date.b: Older releases predate the announcements channel, so the archive dates them from the creation timestamps of the items in them. A tilde marks those dates. They are reliable to the month and not to the day.
term.approx-date.use: A tilde appears on release cards, on release pages and in the archive timeline. Exact dates carry no mark.
term.approx-date.f2: Item creation timestamps in the Highrise catalogue
term.approx-date.f3: Right to the month, not the day
term.approx-date.h1: The archive publishes, with a tilde on every date that predates the announcements channel.
term.trait.p: One feature of a Creature, such as its hair or its outfit.
term.trait.b: Every Creature carries one value in each of thirteen slots, and 466 distinct trait values exist across the collection. The rarer a Creature's values, the higher its rarity rank. Trait values are recorded in the Creature's own metadata, not held by the site.
term.trait.use: Trait means the value, such as Cotton Candy Hair. Slot means the place it sits in. The Traits showcase lists all 466 with the share of the collection wearing each, and every trait page links to the marketplace filtered to it.
term.trait.h1: The Traits showcase publishes all 466 values.
term.slot.p: One of the thirteen places a trait sits on a Creature.
term.slot.b: The thirteen slots are eyes, mouth, nose, ears, hair, head accessory, glasses, face accessory, outfit, body, body accessory, aura and background. Every Creature has a value in each, except the 33 that carry no traits at all.
term.slot.use: Slots are how the Traits showcase and the marketplace filters are organised. Two casing styles appear in the metadata, so the site normalises slot names before matching them.
term.slot.f2: Eyes, mouth, nose, ears, hair, head accessory, glasses, face accessory, outfit, body, body accessory, aura, background
term.slot.h1: All thirteen slots are published in the Traits showcase.
term.outfit.p: A Creature's whole look, counted as one trait rather than several.
term.outfit.b: The outfit slot holds 58 values. Behind each one sit real Highrise garments, a top, bottoms, shoes and so on, which the trait page lists. Twelve looks exist in four variants each, and ten looks belong to the one-of-one characters alone.
term.outfit.use: Outfit is one trait, so filtering by an outfit and filtering by any single garment inside it select the same Creatures.
term.outfit.f2: Twelve looks in four variants, plus ten character looks
term.outfit.h1: The Traits showcase lists every outfit and the garments behind it.
term.piece.p: One of the real Highrise items an outfit is made of.
term.piece.b: A piece belongs to one look and appears in no other. That is why filtering the marketplace by a piece or by the outfit it belongs to selects exactly the same Creatures.
term.piece.use: Pieces are listed on an outfit's trait page. They are Highrise catalogue items in their own right, which is how the site identifies them.
term.one-of-one.p: A Creature drawn as a character rather than assembled from shared traits.
term.one-of-one.b: Ten exist. Their parts belong to them alone, which scores them far above the assembled Creatures and puts all ten at the top of the rarity rank.
term.one-of-one.use: One-of-one describes the Creature, not a rarity tier. The ten hold ranks 1 to 10, which is a tie rather than an order.
term.rarity-tier.p: The word on an item or a Creature that says how scarce it is.
term.rarity-tier.b: Tiers are labels rather than measurements. Which labels apply depends on what is being described: a catalogue item, a garment inside an outfit, a Creature or a LAND parcel each use a different set.
term.rarity-tier.use: A tier chip appears on item cards in the archive, on Creature cards in the marketplace and on LAND parcels. The colour of the chip follows the same scale as its word.
term.rarity-tier.note: Three scales are in use and they do not line up. Items run Common, Rare, Epic, Legendary and Mythical, with no Uncommon. The garments inside an outfit add Uncommon. Creatures run Legendary down to Common and never say Mythical. A LAND parcel's tier is the tier it sold at. So Mythical on an item and Legendary on a Creature are not two rungs of one ladder.
term.rarity-tier.f1: Items: Common, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythical
term.rarity-tier.f2: Creatures: Legendary down to Common, no Mythical
term.rarity-tier.f3: The catalogue for items, the metadata for Creatures, the sale for LAND
term.rarity-rank.p: Where a Creature places among all 11,111 once its traits are scored.
term.rarity-rank.b: The score adds one divided by how common each trait value is, so a single very rare value outweighs several ordinary ones. Rank 1 is the rarest. The rank is worked out from the collection as a whole, so it moves only if the collection does.
term.rarity-rank.use: Rank is shown on Creature cards in the marketplace and on every Creature page. It measures trait scarcity and nothing else: not price, not demand, not tier.
term.rarity-rank.note: Ranks 1 to 10 are a ten-way tie. The ten one-of-ones all score the same and the tie is broken alphabetically, so the order inside the top ten means nothing. A further 33 Creatures carry no traits at all, so there is nothing to score them on and they sit at the bottom.
term.rarity-rank.f2: Score = the sum of 1 divided by each trait value share
term.rarity-rank.h1: Ranks start appearing on Creature cards when the marketplace opens.
term.trait-share.p: How much of the collection wears a trait, as a count and as a percentage of 11,111.
term.trait-share.b: Share is the plainest measure of how rare one trait is, and it is the input the rarity rank is built from. A share under 0.1 per cent is shown as such rather than rounded to zero.
term.trait-share.use: Share appears on every trait page and in the Traits showcase. It counts Creatures, not listings, so it does not move with the market.
term.trait-share.f1: A count out of 11,111, and the same figure as a percentage
term.trait-share.h1: Shares are published for all 466 trait values.
term.nft.p: An item recorded on a blockchain and owned by a wallet rather than by an account.
term.nft.b: Creatures and LAND are NFTs. Ownership is recorded on the chain itself, so an owner can move or sell one without the club taking part and without asking anyone. The club cannot move a holder's asset and never holds it.
term.nft.use: The site uses NFT for the on-chain asset and asset for a Creature or a parcel without saying which. Creature Coins are not NFTs.
term.nft.f1: Creatures on Immutable zkEVM, LAND on Ethereum mainnet
term.nft.f2: The owner's wallet, never the club
term.wallet.p: The app that holds the keys to an address and signs on its owner's behalf.
term.wallet.b: A wallet holds keys, not assets: the assets sit on the chain and the keys prove who may move them. The club never takes custody. Every action on this site's marketplace is signed in the holder's own wallet and can be refused there.
term.wallet.use: Wallet means both the app and the address it controls. The marketplace shows a shortened form of an address, such as 0xCf44 followed by the last four characters.
term.wallet.f2: Every listing, offer, purchase and transfer on this site
term.wallet.h1: The Guides tab opens, with wallet walkthroughs.
term.metamask.p: The wallet most members here use, as a browser extension or a phone app.
term.metamask.b: This site's marketplace talks to MetaMask directly for signing, approvals and network switches. Other wallets that speak the same browser standard work too; MetaMask is what the guides are written against.
term.metamask.use: MetaMask is named in the walkthroughs and in the marketplace guide. The chain it needs to be on depends on the asset: Immutable zkEVM for Creatures, Ethereum mainnet for LAND.
term.token-trove.p: The official marketplace for Creatures away from this site.
term.token-trove.b: Token Trove is where Creatures traded before this site had a marketplace of its own, and it still lists them. This site's marketplace reads the same Immutable orderbook, so a listing made in one is visible in the other.
term.token-trove.use: Token Trove is linked from the Guides tab. It is an outside service, not part of the club.
term.immutable-zkevm.p: The blockchain the Creatures live on.
term.immutable-zkevm.b: It was built for game items, so fees are small and confirmations are quick. Gas there is paid in IMX. The Creature collection moved to it from Immutable StarkEx, which is where the 39-digit token ids come from.
term.immutable-zkevm.use: Creature actions need a wallet on Immutable zkEVM. LAND actions need Ethereum mainnet. The marketplace prompts for the switch rather than assuming it.
term.immutable-zkevm.h1: The Creature collection moves to Immutable zkEVM from Immutable StarkEx.
term.ethereum-mainnet.p: The main Ethereum chain, where LAND lives.
term.ethereum-mainnet.b: Fees on mainnet are far higher than on Immutable zkEVM and are paid in ETH. LAND, estates and LAND deeds are all recorded there, and LAND trades there through OpenSea's Seaport contracts.
term.ethereum-mainnet.use: The site keeps the two chains apart in every screen that involves money, because funds on one cannot pay for anything on the other until they are bridged.
term.bridging.p: Moving funds from one chain to the other.
term.bridging.b: ETH sitting on Ethereum cannot buy a Creature on Immutable zkEVM until it has been bridged across. A bridge takes the funds on one side and releases the matching amount on the other, usually within minutes, through an outside provider.
term.bridging.use: The funding walkthrough covers bridging and tracks a crossing to completion. Bridging is not the same as an on-ramp: a bridge moves crypto already held, an on-ramp buys it with money.
term.bridging.f2: Between Ethereum mainnet and Immutable zkEVM
term.gas.p: The fee a chain charges to record a transaction.
term.gas.b: Gas is paid to the network, not to the club or the marketplace. On Immutable zkEVM it is paid in IMX and is small. On Ethereum mainnet it is paid in ETH and is not. A wallet holding an asset but no gas token cannot transact until it holds some.
term.gas.use: The marketplace names the gas token before asking for a signature, because the token needed depends on the chain the asset is on.
term.gas.f1: IMX on Immutable zkEVM, ETH on Ethereum mainnet
term.gas.f2: Paid to the network, not to the club
term.currencies.p: The four tokens the club's trading touches, and what each one is for.
term.currencies.b: ETH buys Creatures on Immutable zkEVM and LAND on Ethereum mainnet. IMX does one job, paying gas on Immutable zkEVM. USDC is a dollar-pegged alternative to ETH and is accepted across the marketplace on both chains. WETH is ETH wrapped so it can be bid with, and it appears only in LAND offers.
term.currencies.use: Prices are shown in the token they are set in, with a dollar figure beside them. USDC uses six decimals on Immutable zkEVM rather than the eighteen ETH uses, which is why amounts are never converted by hand.
term.currencies.f1: ETH and USDC to buy, IMX for gas, WETH for LAND offers
term.currencies.f2: USDC uses six decimals, ETH and WETH use eighteen
term.listing.p: An asset put up for sale at a price its owner sets.
term.listing.b: A listing is an order signed by the owner and published to the orderbook. The asset stays in the owner's wallet the whole time and moves only when someone fills the order. A listing can be cancelled at any point before that.
term.listing.use: Listings on this site can be priced in ETH or USDC. The site takes no fee on a sale. Listings made here appear on the other marketplaces reading the same orderbook, and theirs appear here.
term.listing.f2: The asset stays in the owner's wallet
term.listing.h1: The Creature and LAND marketplace opens on this site.
term.offer.p: A bid on something that is not for sale, or a lower price on something that is.
term.offer.b: An offer is a signed order in the other direction: the buyer commits funds at a price and the holder may take it or leave it. LAND offers are made in WETH or USDC, since an offer has to be made in a token that can be held in escrow.
term.offer.use: Offers appear on an asset's page and in the holder's own list. Nothing moves until the holder accepts.
term.offer.f3: The holder, by accepting or ignoring it
term.offer.h1: Offers open on this site alongside listings.
term.floor.p: The cheapest one listed right now.
term.floor.b: The floor is a snapshot of the cheapest open listing in a collection, and it changes through the day as listings appear and sell. It says what today's cheapest seller wants, not what any particular asset is worth.
term.floor.use: The Market tab charts the floor over time alongside sales. A floor is per collection, so Creatures and LAND have their own.
term.floor.f1: The live orderbook, read through the day
term.floor.h1: The Market tab publishes live floor prices and sale history.
term.all-in-price.p: The asking price plus every fee and royalty, so nothing is hidden at signing.
term.all-in-price.b: The all-in price is what actually leaves a buyer's wallet. This site charges no marketplace fee on a Creature sale. LAND sales carry the creator royalty and the OpenSea fee that Seaport enforces on mainnet, and both are counted in before the buyer signs.
term.all-in-price.use: The all-in figure is shown next to the asking price wherever a purchase is confirmed, so a listing cannot look cheaper than it is.
term.all-in-price.f1: No marketplace fee on this site
term.all-in-price.f2: LAND on mainnet also carries a creator royalty and the marketplace fee Seaport enforces
term.all-in-price.f3: Gas is separate and paid to the network
term.all-in-price.h1: Every purchase on this site starts showing its all-in price.
term.approval.p: A one-time signature letting a marketplace contract move one specific asset when it sells.
term.approval.b: An approval hands nothing over and spends nothing by itself. It authorises the contract to transfer that asset if, and only if, an order the owner signed is filled. It can be revoked in the wallet.
term.approval.use: The marketplace asks for an approval the first time an asset is listed, then not again for that asset. A request to approve anything else is worth reading twice.
term.approval.h1: Listing on this site starts asking for a per-asset approval.
term.mint.p: Creating the on-chain item for the first time.
term.mint.b: For LAND, minting is what turns a deed into the parcel it stands for. For the Creatures, minting was the original November 2021 issuance of all 11,111.
term.mint.use: Mint is used for the act and for the moment: the mint refers to the 2021 issuance, minting a deed refers to a single transaction a holder signs today.
term.mint.f1: Deeds today, and the 2021 Creature issuance
term.on-ramp.p: Buying crypto with a card or a phone wallet, so a purchase needs no crypto up front.
term.on-ramp.b: An on-ramp is run by an outside provider, which takes the payment, does its own checks and delivers the crypto to the buyer's wallet. The club neither takes the money nor sees the card.
term.on-ramp.use: The on-ramp appears at the point a purchase needs funds it cannot see. The session is created when the button is pressed and expires in minutes, so its link is never reusable.
term.on-ramp.f1: An outside provider, not the club
term.cash-out.p: Turning a sale back into money in a bank account.
term.cash-out.b: Cashing out runs through the same kind of outside provider as an on-ramp, in the other direction: crypto in, bank transfer out, with the provider's own checks in between.
term.cash-out.use: Cash out names the button in the marketplace as well as the act. Timing and limits belong to the provider, not to the club.
term.cash-out.f1: An outside provider, not the club
term.seed-phrase.p: The words that restore a wallet, and with it everything the wallet holds.
term.seed-phrase.b: A seed phrase is not a password and cannot be reset. Anyone who reads it controls the wallet from then on, on every chain at once, with no way to undo it.
term.seed-phrase.use: It is typed once, into the wallet app, when a wallet is first restored. No other screen ever has a reason to ask for it.
term.seed-phrase.note: No admin, no team member and no website will ever need a seed phrase. That includes this one. A request for it is a theft in progress, whatever the reason given.
term.seed-phrase.f1: Every asset in the wallet, on every chain
term.seed-phrase.h1: Scam Watch publishes the tactics seen in the club, seed phrase theft among them.
term.token-id.p: The chain's own name for a Creature, a 39-digit number.
term.token-id.b: A Creature has two identifiers. The number in its name, such as 3379, is the one holders say and the one its page is addressed by. Its token id is a 39-digit number left over from the move off Immutable StarkEx. Both point at the same Creature and the site accepts either.
term.token-id.use: Token ids appear in contract calls and block explorers. Creature numbers appear everywhere else, including the marketplace and this codex.
term.token-id.f1: A 39-digit number, mapped one to one to the Creature number
term.token-id.f2: Left over from the StarkEx to zkEVM move
term.token-id.h1: The move to Immutable zkEVM leaves every Creature with a 39-digit token id.
term.player-council.p: A holder-led group of seven that works with the club on Gen 2 and the steady drops.
term.player-council.b: The Council is advisory: a say on creative direction and the roadmap, not a vote on the business. Pocket Worlds keeps final say. Seven seats exist, four elected by holders and three appointed for continuity, two of those by Pocket Worlds and one from the holders. Elected terms run six months, two in a row at most.
term.player-council.use: Council means the body. A seat is a formal role on top of membership, and it cannot be bought, sold or transferred. Every holder is a club member whether or not they hold a seat.
term.player-council.f2: Six months for an elected seat, two consecutive terms at most
term.player-council.h2: The appointed seats are named and the election dates set.
term.player-council.h5: The second meeting settles that Creature Coins stay untradable.
term.election.p: How the four elected Council seats get filled.
term.election.b: Holders self-nominate, answer the same open questions and are voted on by holders, one vote per seat. The four elected seats sit in three brackets by holding size: two for holders of one to four assets, one for holders of five to fourteen, and one for holders of fifteen or more, so the largest holders cannot take every seat. Votes are never weighted by how much a voter holds.
term.election.use: The election runs in phases and the site follows them: nominations, then voting, then results. The Council tab holds all three.
term.election.f2: Holders of one asset or more, held for three months
term.election.f3: One holder, one vote per seat, never weighted by holdings

term.election.h3: The results are published and the first Council is seated.
term.ballot.p: The official vote, cast once per holder per seat.
term.ballot.b: A voter signs in with the Discord account linked to their Highrise profile, the site checks their linked wallet against the electorate snapshot, and the vote is recorded against both the account and the wallet so neither can vote twice. The voter gets a private receipt code. Individual votes are never published, only the per-seat tallies.
term.ballot.use: Ballot means the official vote. A poll on the Polls and Votes tab is a separate thing: holder-gated, but not an election.
term.ballot.f1: One vote per account and per wallet, in each seat race
term.ballot.f2: Discord sign-in, plus the linked wallet checked against the snapshot
term.ballot.f3: Tallies published per seat, individual votes never
term.ballot.h2: The per-seat tallies are published with the results.
term.confirmation-vote.p: What a seat race gets when it has no more candidates than places.
term.confirmation-vote.b: Rather than choosing between people, voters either confirm the candidate or vote to reopen nominations and invite challengers. If reopening wins and nobody new stands, the original candidate takes the seat. A seat can be contested; it cannot be blocked into a vacancy.
term.confirmation-vote.use: The ballot switches to this form on its own when a race is uncontested, and says so on the seat.
term.confirmation-vote.f1: Any seat race with candidates equal to or fewer than its places
term.electorate-snapshot.p: The list of who may vote, frozen before voting opens.
term.electorate-snapshot.b: Eligibility is read from the two contracts and then fixed, so the electorate cannot change while a vote is running. Freezing it stops anyone buying a vote after seeing the candidates, and stops a sale mid-vote from taking one away.
term.electorate-snapshot.use: The snapshot is what the ballot checks a wallet against. Addresses in it are stored in lower case, so a wallet is matched regardless of how it is written.
term.electorate-snapshot.f1: The Creature and LAND contracts, read once
term.electorate-snapshot.f2: Frozen before voting opens, unchanged until it closes
term.electorate-snapshot.f3: Holders of three months or more
term.electorate-snapshot.h1: The first electorate is frozen before voting opens.
term.voting-advice.p: A tool that matches a holder's own answers against what the candidates said.
term.voting-advice.b: Every candidate answers the same open questions. The tool asks a voter the same statements, compares the two and ranks the candidates by agreement. It casts no vote and it publishes its method, so a result can be checked rather than trusted.
term.voting-advice.use: The matcher sits beside the ballot and is optional. Its ranking is advice; the ballot is the vote.
term.voting-advice.h1: The voting advice matcher goes live with nominations.
